questions.prompt: Design A: 78/520 sign-ups. Design B: 51/480. Compute the POOLED proportion p̄ (3 decimals).
Comparing two teams' variability: s₁ = 2.4 (n₁ = 10), s₂ = 1.3 (n₂ = 12). The F statistic and df are:
options: F₀ = 2.4²/1.3² = 3.408 with df = (9, 11) — LARGER variance on top
questions.explain: **Larger variance in the numerator** ⇒ F₀ = 5.76/1.69 = **3.408**, df₁ = 10−1 = 9, df₂ = 12−1 = 11. Two-tailed at α = 0.05 → use the **α/2 = 0.025** right-tail table: F(0.025; 9, 11) = 3.59 → 3.408 < 3.59 → fail to reject (borderline trap!).

questions.prompt: n₁ = 12, s₁² = 26.01; n₂ = 10, s₂² = 21.16. Compute the pooled variance s_p² = [(n₁−1)s₁² + (n₂−1)s₂²]/(n₁+n₂−2) (3 decimals).

questions.source: Drill CH5 P10 — paired or not?
questions.prompt: The SAME 8 pages are measured before and after an optimization. Which test, and why?
options: Paired t-test — the same units are measured twice, so analyze the differences D
questions.explain: Same pages twice = **dependent samples → paired t**. D = before − after; 'reduced' ⇒ D > 0 ⇒ H₁: μ_D > 0 (right-tailed). The paired t is the **guaranteed exam archetype** (appears in 8/8 papers).

questions.source: Drill CH5 P10 — the t statistic
questions.prompt: D̄ = 0.488, s_D = 0.290, n = 8. Compute t₀ = D̄/(s_D/√n) (2 decimals).
questions.explain: t₀ = 0.488/(0.290/√8) = 0.488/0.1025 = **4.754**, df = 7. Critical t(0.05, 7) = 1.895 → 4.754 > 1.895 → **reject H₀**: 'At α = 0.05 there is sufficient evidence that the optimization reduced mean page load time.' (Defining D = after−before flips all signs — same conclusion if consistent.)

questions.prompt: Match: independent samples, σ's unknown but assumed equal → ? · same subjects twice → ? · comparing two proportions → ?
options: Pooled t (df = n₁+n₂−2) · paired t (df = n−1 pairs) · two-proportion z with pooled p̄
questions.explain: The Q2 selection table: **independent + equal variances → pooled t**; **dependent/same units → paired t**; **two proportions → z with pooled p̄**; **two variances → F (larger on top)**. Choosing the right test is the first 2 marks.
